title: After 1973 and Alberta Hunter's 'not bitchy enough' advice
summary: Dance says the 1973 comeback showed more of Humes than her R&B hits. Humes recounts Alberta Hunter telling her she was not bitchy enough and stories of Hunter and another singer rebuking talkative audiences.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: In fact, you haven't told us about, and we haven't come to that yet and we're going to talk about that, '73 on. But one thing we ought to say about it is, it's not only that you made a comeback and were bigger in your career than ever before but it was different, I think, wasn't it? It is like your horizons were broadened. I mean, for a time like in the late '40s and early '50s when R. and B. was big and you did "Ebobaleeba" and you did "Million Dollar Secret". You were a big star like other stars then. But it didn't show what your whole capabilities were.

Yeah, well you know people tell me, just like Alberta Hunter, "you know, you aint bitchyenough". I said, "what?" She said, "you aint bitchy enough". I said, "well, what do I have to do?" She said, "you just ought to lay everybody out and let them know you're this and you're that and you're the other". I said, "Oh shucks, if they don't know what I am I don't know what to tell them, and if I've got to be bitchy then I'll just forget about the singing".
She'd lay you out in a minute. One time she was singing and this lady was a news reporter.

But she didn't know it then. And the lady was just writing down, you know, things, and writing down the songs that she sang. Alberta stopped singing and she said, "now look, I want to tell you this. There is no need for you to sit up here trying to copy my work because that's what you always do". And she said, "because I got my song's copyrighted and there ain't nothing you can do about it". Well the woman was just giving her a write-up, you know? I said, well I guess that's what she means by being bitchy. I saw alot of them like that.

And a friend of mine was working in the court one time and you know, they was having a big night there and when she got through singing, everybody was busy getting themselves together. And so she made an announcement. She said, "well, I decided not to come here because I had some work done on my teeth and I didn't feel like singing." But she said, "I had made this engagement and I said, I would just keep it. But I'm saying that to say this, I don't think you should be fucking around while I'm singing."
